s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent gross hematuria in a patient with a history of pelvic surgery and radiation
salient_findings: Pulsatile arterial bleeding from the right ureteral orifice
key_facts: Treated with liver metastasectomy, Hartmann’s procedure, and intraoperative radiotherapy
Adjuvant chemotherapy with capecitabine, oxaliplatin, and bevacizumab
Bilateral JJ stents for ureteral strictures since December 2009
CT angiogram demonstrated active hemorrhage at the right renal pelvis
Embolisation of the right renal artery with coils
Recurrent gross hematuria despite transfusion and embolisation

raw.syndrome_frame: Recurrent gross hematuria in a patient with a history of pelvic surgery and radiation
salient_findings: Pulsatile arterial bleeding from the right ureteral orifice
key_facts: Treated with liver metastasectomy, Hartmann’s procedure, and intraoperative radiotherapy
Adjuvant chemotherapy with capecitabine, oxaliplatin, and bevacizumab
Bilateral JJ stents for ureteral strictures since December 2009
CT angiogram demonstrated active hemorrhage at the right renal pelvis
Embolisation of the right renal artery with coils
Recurrent gross hematuria despite transfusion and embolisation

differentials: Fistula between ureter and iliac vessels
per_call: Fistula between ureter and iliac vessels

shortlist.label: Radiation cystitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of pelvic radiation and recurrent gross hematuria

shortlist.label: Ureteroenteric fistula
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed by retrograde ureterography and consistent with clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Arteriovenous fistula
shortlist.why_kept: Pulsatile arterial bleeding from the right ureteral orifice and recurrent hematuria

shortlist.label: Pseudoaneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Embolisation of the right renal artery with coils and recurrent hematuria

shortlist.label: Ureteral stricture
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral JJ stents for ureteral strictures since December 2009 and recurrent hematuria

raw.rationale: The patient's history of intraoperative radiotherapy and subsequent development of hematuria, ureteral strictures, and hydronephrosis are consistent with radiation-induced damage to the urinary tract, which is a hallmark of radiation cystitis.

rejected.label: Ureteroenteric fistula
rejected.why: Although a ureteroileal fistula was found, it does not fully explain the patient's initial presentation of gross hematuria and the presence of active hemorrhage at the right renal pelvis.

rejected.label: Arteriovenous fistula
rejected.why: There is no direct evidence of an arteriovenous fistula, and the patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with radiation-induced damage.

rejected.label: Pseudoaneurysm
rejected.why: The CT angiogram demonstrated active hemorrhage, but there is no mention of a pseudoaneurysm, and the patient's history and symptoms are more consistent with radiation cystitis.

rejected.label: Ureteral stricture
rejected.why: While the patient has ureteral strictures, this alone does not explain the active hemorrhage and gross hematuria, which are more consistent with radiation cystitis.
